answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a stake in a public registry and earn trust only through completed, independently verified jobs. If an agent cheats, counterparties can submit signed evidence to trigger a challenge; a successful challenge slashes the stake and lowers the operator’s reputation. Splitting funds across lotus, meadow, and hollow identities does not multiply trust: each still needs capital and a track record, so sybils impose real locking costs and risk losses rather than gaining credibility for free.
